purpose: Run an outcome-blind design sensitivity analysis for the number of independent confirmation evidence contexts before any context manifest, model output, label, detector score, or confirmation metric exists.

allowed_inputs: aggregate source-capacity counts from the completed context-feasibility proof
forbidden_inputs: historical detector performance used to calibrate synthetic score separation
review_boundary.interpretation: This is a planning sensitivity analysis, not a formal power calculation, detector evaluation, or guarantee of future confidence-interval coverage.

synthetic_data_model.average_precision_definition: Average precision computed from the ranked synthetic unsupported-risk scores.
synthetic_data_model.cluster_label_model: For each context, draw a context-specific prevalence from a beta distribution parameterized by the scenario prevalence and label ICC, then draw binary span labels conditionally within that context.
synthetic_data_model.cluster_size_model: Use a deterministic five-context multiplier pattern of 0.65, 0.85, 1.00, 1.15, and 1.35 around each scenario mean, with a minimum of four spans. This tests unequal cluster sizes without using observed confirmation data.
synthetic_data_model.paired_score_model: Generate two correlated synthetic risk scores from shared and detector-specific Gaussian noise. Detector B has a fixed 0.20 standardized separation increment only to study paired-difference interval width; it is not a predicted evidence-aware advantage.

monte_carlo.paired_resampling: The same resampled context indices are used for both synthetic detector scores.

decision_policy.selection_rule: Select the smallest balanced candidate that satisfies every structural and central-scenario rule. Stress scenarios are disclosure checks and cannot be hidden, but they are not pass criteria because the source cannot guarantee their future prevalence or cluster structure.
decision_policy.failure_rule: If no candidate passes, do not create a context manifest. Revise the study scope, acquire additional independent contexts, or explicitly downgrade the planned claim before proceeding.

future_interval_policy.planned_primary_interval: context-level BCa bootstrap when all leave-one-context-out estimates are defined
future_interval_policy.small_cluster_caveat: Fewer than 30 independent contexts remains a small-cluster setting. Report intervals and avoid a binary superiority claim when the interval is wide or interval methods disagree.

literature_context.title: Simple Approaches for Dealing With Correlated Data
literature_context.relevance: Supports resampling whole clusters and cautions that clustered-bootstrap validity still relies on large-sample arguments, with particular caution below 30 clusters.

literature_context.title: Pointwise sampling uncertainties on the Precision-Recall curve
literature_context.relevance: Shows that PR uncertainty depends on test-set sampling and that scarce positives can create discrete bootstrap behavior.

literature_context.title: Estimating Uncertainty in Classifier Performance with Applications to Large Language Models and Nested Data
literature_context.relevance: Recent preprint evidence that default intervals can under-cover for small nested text-classification evaluations; used as a caution, not as a settled standard.

allowed: candidate design pass or fail status
forbidden: new empirical AUPRC or F1 claims
